evals.prompt: This vendor calls its offering a product, but every customer I've spoken to spent four months tuning it. What evolution stage is it really at, and what does that mean for how we should run the project?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Places the component in one Wardley evolution stage with a named label; Anchors the placement in observable evidence such as integration time or reference-customer count; States the way of working the stage implies; Flags the mismatch between the vendor's product framing and bespoke integration.
expectations: Places the component in one Wardley evolution stage with a named label
Anchors the placement in observable evidence such as integration time or reference-customer count
States the way of working the stage implies
Flags the mismatch between the vendor's product framing and bespoke integration

evals.prompt: Half of these tools are bespoke one-offs and half are off-the-shelf utilities, but our brief compares them all the same way. Tag each technology with where it sits in its lifecycle so the comparison stops being apples to oranges.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Assigns exactly one evolution stage per named component; Notes that components at different stages need different ways of working; Recommends utility treatment for commodity components and time-boxed experiments for novel ones.
expectations: Assigns exactly one evolution stage per named component
Notes that components at different stages need different ways of working
Recommends utility treatment for commodity components and time-boxed experiments for novel ones

evals.prompt: Is this capability genesis, custom built, product or commodity? Give me the Wardley evolution stage with a rationale I can defend to the architecture board.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Uses the four Wardley stage labels; Gives a one-line rationale citing something countable or checkable; Marks the placement as an estimate when only vendor self-positioning supports it.
expectations: Uses the four Wardley stage labels
Gives a one-line rationale citing something countable or checkable
Marks the placement as an estimate when only vendor self-positioning supports it

evals.prompt: Map our whole value chain from the end-user need down through every supporting component so I can see the dependencies and where to focus.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Anchors on the user need and lays out a full value chain with dependencies; Does not stop at scoring a single component.
expectations: Anchors on the user need and lays out a full value chain with dependencies
Does not stop at scoring a single component

evals.prompt: How much deployment evidence exists for this inference accelerator? I need the readiness level with the proof at each level before we commit.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Assesses maturity against a cumulative evidence-gated readiness scale; Does not assign a build-buy-rent strategic stage.
expectations: Assesses maturity against a cumulative evidence-gated readiness scale
Does not assign a build-buy-rent strategic stage
